name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that A.R.S. § 12-516(A) violates the anti-abrogation clause by eliminating a patient's right to recover damages for ordinary negligence, as gross negligence is not a reasonable alternative.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred with the main judgment, agreeing that A.R.S. § 12-516(A) is unconstitutional, and also concurred with the rejection of arguments regarding inherent emergency powers and derivative sovereign immunity.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented from the judgment, arguing that the anti-abrogation clause does not invalidate the statute that increases the standard for proving negligence in COVID-19 cases, but concurred with the rejection of arguments regarding inherent emergency powers and derivative sovereign immunity.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, arguing that the initiative proposes a law by creating public policy to preserve Lake Powell Boulevard and preventing public funds from narrowing it, thus falling within legislative authority.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the court, arguing that A.R.S. § 19-121.04(A) is unconstitutional as applied because its double counting mechanism effectively raised the constitutional 15% signature threshold for initiatives, violating both the Arizona and United States Constitutions.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, authored the opinion, concluding that the geographic voting districts for court of appeals judges do not violate the Free and Equal Elections Clause or the Equal Privileges and Immunities Clause of the Arizona Constitution, as there is no constitutional right to vote in every court of appeals judge's retention election and the one-person, one-vote principle does not apply to the judiciary.

name: Jennifer M. Perkins
description: Concurred, delivered the decision of the Court, finding the offering was exempt from registration, some fraud claims were puffery or had a reasonable basis, but upholding the fraud finding for personal use of funds.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, authored the opinion that Arizona law does not permit FDA warnings to substitute for expert testimony to establish the standard of care.

name: BOLICK, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the failure to follow a black box warning should present a prima facie case of negligent failure to warn, believing the dismissal inappropriately deprived the plaintiffs of their day in court.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature intended to hold GEI defendants criminally responsible for their actions, making them liable for victim restitution, and overruled Heartfield.

name: Justice Bolick
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the court, finding that release time provisions violate the Gift Clause but not free-speech, free-association, or right-to-work rights.

name: JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, arguing that the 2018 legislative amendments reclassified desegregation expenses as a new type of secondary property tax not eligible for state reimbursement, and these amendments are constitutional.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that a prosecutor's conflict of interest erodes confidence in the judicial system and that trial courts must apply Gomez factors when considering disqualification, also emphasizing the need to assess defendant's due process rights and victim's rights.

name: TIMMER, VICE CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that a higher bid is relevant but not conclusive for Gift Clause analysis, and non-pecuniary factors are important. Also, found disputed facts regarding the City's discretion in canceling the RFP, requiring remand.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the Condominium Act did not unconstitutionally take property as the Xias contractually agreed to its terms, but that the Act required the sale of the entire condominium, not just individual units, in a forced termination.

name: JUSTICE KING
description: Concurred, argued that the State has a right to appeal expungement orders affecting its substantial rights under § 13-4032(4), and § 36-2862(F) does not preclude this right.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that § 36-2322 does not create an independent right to abortion or repeal § 13-3603, and that with Roe overturned, § 13-3603 is now enforceable.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that § 36-2322(B) and § 13-3603 should be harmonized to permit abortions before fifteen weeks' gestation or to preserve the pregnant woman's health, and that the majority incorrectly used a construction note to create ambiguity.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, argued that the anti-abrogation clause does not extend to dram-shop actions because they were recognized after statehood.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the decision correctly upholds legislative authority in tort law and prevents the judiciary from overstepping its bounds by creating new liabilities.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the anti-abrogation clause protects common law actions as they evolve, including dram-shop actions, and the legislature's limitation unconstitutionally abrogates this right.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented in part and in the result, arguing that the majority's 'substantial probability' standard for direct disclosure is an additional, inconsistent requirement that impermissibly diminishes a defendant's ability to exercise a federal constitutional right, and that the 'reasonable possibility' standard should apply consistently.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented in part and in the result, arguing that the majority's 'substantial probability' standard for direct disclosure is an additional, inconsistent requirement that impermissibly diminishes a defendant's ability to exercise a federal constitutional right, and that the 'reasonable possibility' standard should apply consistently.

name: BOLICK, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, authored the opinion holding that the court of appeals had jurisdiction over the appeals.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that before a defendant's right to appeal can be abrogated under § 13-4033(C), the defendant must receive notice that the right may be waived, the waiver must be knowing, intelligent, and voluntary, and the defendant must be provided an opportunity at sentencing to prove their absence was involuntary. The court also found § 13-4033(C) constitutional and not in conflict with court rules.

name: BOLICK, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that A.R.S. § 23-1043.01(B) is constitutional because the original public meaning of "injury by accident" in the Arizona Constitution did not encompass mental stress injuries, and the legislature permissibly expanded workers' compensation within limits.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that A.R.S. § 23-1043.01(B) violates Article 18, Section 8 of the Arizona Constitution because "injury" and "personal injury" should be interpreted to include mental injuries, and the statute impermissibly restricts legal causation.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the Arizona Constitution grants individual commissioners the power to inspect and investigate public service corporations, and a majority cannot prevent this.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission did not prevent Burns from exercising his investigatory powers, as his actions were part of a contested rate case subject to Commission authority, not a solitary investigation.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that the Secretary of State's flawed electronic registration process made it impossible for circulators to comply with the affidavit requirement, and disqualifying signatures would unconstitutionally hinder the initiative process.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that tax revenue measures for the support and maintenance of state departments and institutions are exempt from referendum, regardless of whether they increase or decrease revenue, based on the plain text of the Arizona Constitution.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that tax revenue measures should only be exempt from referendum if they comply with all constitutional requirements for emergency measures, and that the majority's interpretation undermines the people's reserved referendum power.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part with Justice Montgomery's opinion.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Authored the Opinion of the Court, arguing that legislative privilege protects the Senate's audit communications as a legitimate legislative activity, but administrative and political communications must be disclosed.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, argued that the Arizona Constitution guarantees due process rights for individuals under grand jury investigation, requiring prosecutors to present clearly exculpatory evidence, including that related to justification defenses, to ensure a fair and impartial grand jury proceeding.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court affirming Robinson's convictions and sentences.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that attorney fees are recoverable as restitution only when reasonably necessary to remedy the harm directly caused by criminal conduct, and most of C.C.'s fees were not directly caused by Reed's conduct.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged budget reconciliation bills violated the Arizona Constitution's title requirement and single subject rule because their substantive provisions lacked a natural connection to their titles and budgetary purpose.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the "manageable standards" inquiry in the political question context is not constitutionally mandated and abdicates the judiciary's central role in determining constitutional boundaries.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that crime victims have a constitutional and statutory right to be heard on a defendant's motion for a delayed appeal of a restitution order, as it implicates their rights to due process, prompt restitution, and finality.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision improperly expands victim rights beyond what is legally established, effectively granting them party status not intended by law.

name: Justice Andrew W. Gould (Ret.)
description: Participated in oral argument but retired before issuance of this opinion and did not take part in its drafting.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, finding Prop. 208's direct funding unconstitutional if it exceeds expenditure limits and that the Tax Enactment Clause does not apply to voter initiatives.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreeing with the denial of the preliminary injunction but disagreeing with the majority's severability analysis and the framework for determining unconstitutionality, arguing it almost certainly dooms the measure.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, arguing that Arizona's legislature has not expressly or unequivocally consented to federal damages liability under the FLSA.

name: Justice Andrew W. Gould (Ret.)
description: Did not take part in the drafting or issuance of the opinion due to retirement.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that a standard of care expert affidavit is not required for ineffective assistance of counsel claims, Perry v. New Hampshire did not constitute a significant change in Arizona law, and A.R.S. § 13-4234(G) unconstitutionally conflicts with Arizona Rule of Criminal Procedure 32.4 by curtailing the right to appeal for IAC claims.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that Mesnard is immune for the investigatory report as it was a legislative function, but not for the news release which was a political act.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the case should be resolved on political question grounds, not speech or debate grounds, because the Constitution commits disciplinary functions solely to the legislature, making it nonjusticiable.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutional right to restitution guarantees the full amount of economic loss or injury, rendering the statutory limitation unconstitutional.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that the home rule charter provision grants charter cities autonomy over purely municipal concerns like election scheduling, making the state law inapplicable.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented, argued that the home rule charter provision clearly states city charters are subject to state laws, and the majority's interpretation is a misreading of the Constitution.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, arguing that the City's payments to a private entity for economic development violated the Gift Clause because the value received by the public was far exceeded by the consideration paid, constituting an impermissible subsidy.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that neither the federal nor Arizona Constitution requires a search warrant or court order to obtain IP addresses and ISP subscriber information, as this information is not considered a 'private affair' under the third-party doctrine.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented, argued that the Arizona Constitution's private affairs clause provides broader protections than the Fourth Amendment and requires a warrant or court order for IP addresses and ISP subscriber information, as such information constitutes 'private affairs'.
